# The Pipe

Two pipe operators are common in R:

* `%>%` from the `magrittr` package (loaded with `tidyverse`/`dplyr`)
* `|>` the base-R native pipe

RStudio shortcut: **Ctrl+Shift+M**.

Why bother? Because `f(g(h(x)))` reads inside-out, while
`x %>% h() %>% g() %>% f()` reads left to right, in the order things
actually happen.

```{r message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

iris %>% group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(Petal.Width), .groups = "drop")

Gender <- factor(c("Female", "Male", "Male", "Female", "Female", "Male"))

Gender %>% table() %>% data.frame() %>%
  rename("Gender" = 1, Count = Freq) %>%
  mutate(Rel_freq = round(Count / sum(Count), 2)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Gender, y = Rel_freq)) + geom_col()
```

Without the pipe, the same computation nests inside-out:
```{r}
summarise(group_by(iris, Species), mean = mean(Petal.Width))
```

# Data Manipulation with `tidyverse`

Loading `tidyverse` pulls in several packages at once: `ggplot2`, `tibble`,
`tidyr`, `readr`, `purrr`, `dplyr`, `stringr`, `forcats`, and `lubridate`.
There's no need to load each individually afterward.

## `dplyr`

Grammar-based data manipulation — see Chapter 10 for the core verbs
(`select`, `filter`, `arrange`, `rename`, `mutate`, `summarise`).

## `tibble`

A tibble is a modernized data frame: cleaner printing, no silent partial
matching, and no automatic factor conversion.
```{r}
library(tibble)
tb <- as_tibble(iris)
tb
glimpse(tb)
```

## `reshape2`

Reshaping data between wide and long formats:
```{r message=FALSE, fig.height=3, fig.width=8}
library(reshape2)
library(tidyr)

view1 <- iris %>% group_by(Species) %>%
  summarise_if(is.numeric, list(mean = mean, sd = sd)) %>%
  melt(id.vars = "Species") %>%
  separate(variable, into = c("variable", "metric"), sep = "_")

view1
```

Pivoting back to wide format with `tidyr::pivot_wider()`:
```{r}
view2 <- view1 %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(std_error = sd / sqrt(nrow(iris)))
view2
```

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=8}
view2 %>% ggplot() +
  geom_bar(aes(x = Species, y = mean), stat = "identity", fill = "forestgreen", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(x = Species, ymin = mean - std_error, ymax = mean + std_error),
                width = 0.4, colour = "orange", alpha = 0.9, linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, ncol = 4)
```

# Presenting Tables

## `kableExtra`
Great for styling `knitr::kable()` tables in HTML/PDF reports — see the
[kableExtra cookbook chapter](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/kableextra.html).

## `flextable`
Produces polished tables that also render well in Word documents:
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(broom)
library(flextable)

set.seed(123)
x <- rnorm(100, mean = 5, sd = 1.5)
z <- 4 + 8 * x + rnorm(100)
LR <- lm(z ~ x)

tidy(LR) %>% select(-statistic) %>% flextable() %>% autofit() %>% theme_box()
```

See the [Epi R Handbook tables chapter](https://epirhandbook.com/en/new_pages/tables_presentation.html)
for more `flextable` recipes.

## `officer`
Generates and edits Word/PowerPoint files directly from R — see the
[officeverse guide](https://ardata-fr.github.io/officeverse/) for details.
